title: Employee Ownership Journey
description: Explore employee ownership for your business: clarify what you want from a transition, explore potential paths, and prepare a plan to discuss with qualified professional advisors. Transcribed verbatim from the pinned journey truth (Employee Ownership Journey v0.2 - Optimized Guided Journey.md); stages 14-19 scenario and team screens are content nodes whose detail the scenario engine and review-package export own. PROVISIONAL CONTENT: the pros/cons copy on choices below is draft tradeoff framing authored for the decision-experience rework — it is balanced and factual by rule, never a recommendation, and remains provisional until the advisor content review gate signs it off.
source: Employee Ownership Journey v0.2 - Optimized Guided Journey.md

nodes.title: Explore Employee Ownership for Your Business
nodes.body:
This guided journey will help you clarify what you want from a business transition, explore potential paths, and prepare a plan to discuss with qualified professional advisors.

Important: The platform does not provide legal, tax, investment, valuation, lending, or other professional advice. Your results are exploratory and are designed to help you communicate your goals and have more productive conversations with your professional advisors.

nodes.title: What are you hoping to accomplish?

question.text: What are you hoping to accomplish?
question.why_we_ask: Your selection establishes the initial Owner Objective. The journey does not ask about ESOPs or other structures yet.

choices.label: Get substantial cash at closing
pros: Cash now — simplest to reinvest or diversify
A clean break at closing
cons: Future upside if the company keeps growing is given up
Your role ends unless separately contracted

choices.label: Create income over time
pros: Predictable personal cash flow for years
Retains upside during the payout period
cons: Depends on the buyer's continued performance
Inflation erodes fixed payments; exit is delayed

choices.label: Have my employees own the company
pros: Legacy and culture are preserved
Employees gain a real stake
cons: Slowest path to personal liquidity
Requires transition capital and governance setup

choices.label: I'm not sure. Help me explore

nodes.title: Besides your main goal, what else matters to you?

question.text: Besides your main goal, what else matters to you?
question.why_we_ask: This captures your secondary objectives without forcing you to rank everything.

nodes.title: Put your priorities in order.

question.text: Put your priorities in order.
question.why_we_ask: Ranking the items you selected creates your Secondary Priorities. There is no ranking of irrelevant choices.

nodes.title: Which of your objectives are nonnegotiable?

question.text: Which of your objectives are nonnegotiable?
question.why_we_ask: For each selected objective or important preference: marking it nonnegotiable means it is a must-have for you to move forward. Anything you do not mark remains a preference. The system distinguishes nonnegotiable, strong preference, and preference — and a nonnegotiable is never silently relaxed, ignored, or overridden.

nodes.title: Are there outcomes you want to avoid?

question.text: Are there outcomes you want to avoid?
question.why_we_ask: This creates your negative constraints — the platform now knows not only what you want, but also what you do not want.

choices.label: Losing employee ownership
pros: Scenarios preserve employee-ownership paths
cons: Exits that trade ownership for speed or certainty are excluded

choices.label: Selling to an outside buyer
pros: Exploration stays with employee, management, and community paths
cons: Outside buyers are often the highest-priced bidders — top-of-market exits are excluded

choices.label: Remaining involved long-term
pros: Scenarios keep your exit timeline short
cons: Structures that reward a long transition tenure are excluded

choices.label: Taking on excessive debt
pros: Scenarios favor lower-leverage structures
cons: Debt-financed paths — which can preserve more ownership — are constrained

choices.label: Waiting many years for proceeds
pros: Paths that front-load value are favored
cons: Deferred-payment structures that can raise the total are constrained

choices.label: Disrupting employees
pros: Scenarios weigh workforce continuity heavily
cons: Restructurings that might raise value but disturb roles are excluded

choices.label: Moving the company
pros: Scenarios keep the business in place
cons: Paths that assume relocation are excluded

choices.label: Losing control too quickly
pros: Staged transitions that keep you in charge longer are favored
cons: Fast, clean-break handovers are constrained

choices.label: Taking on unfamiliar partners
pros: Exploration favors known counterparties
cons: Institutional or private-equity capital sources are constrained

nodes.title: When would you ideally like the transition to happen?

question.text: When would you ideally like the transition to happen?

choices.label: Within 1 year
pros: Fastest route to your goal — momentum and a known date
cons: Little preparation time; fewer paths may fit the deadline

choices.label: 1-3 years
pros: Time to prepare the business while keeping a clear clock
cons: Some personal plans wait on the transition

choices.label: 3-5 years
pros: The longest runway — value and readiness can compound before a sale
cons: Proceeds and role changes arrive later

nodes.title: Is this timing nonnegotiable?

question.text: Is this timing nonnegotiable?
question.why_we_ask: If yes, timing becomes a hard constraint.

choices.label: Yes
pros: Timing becomes a hard constraint every scenario must fit
cons: Paths that need longer are excluded, even when they fit you otherwise

choices.label: No
pros: Scenarios may trade timing for value or structure
cons: Suggested paths may carry dates well outside your ideal

nodes.title: After the transaction, how involved would you like to be?

question.text: After the transaction, how involved would you like to be?

choices.label: I want to leave completely
pros: A clean break — your time is fully yours at closing
cons: Continuity rests on the team and the structure; your knowledge must transfer

choices.label: I could stay temporarily
pros: You can steady the handover without a long commitment
cons: A defined exit date still arrives — and can be hard to extend

choices.label: I'd like to remain involved
pros: An ongoing role, income, and influence in the company's future
cons: Liquidity and freedom arrive gradually rather than at closing

nodes.title: How long would you be comfortable remaining involved?

question.text: How long would you be comfortable remaining involved?

choices.label: Less than 6 months
pros: The shortest handover commitment
cons: Very short tenures can strain continuity and buyer confidence

choices.label: 6-18 months
pros: Enough time for a structured handover with a clear end
cons: Your commitment spans one to two business cycles

choices.label: 18+ months
pros: Maximum continuity — time to mentor successors and protect value
cons: Your exit stretches over years; full liquidity is furthest away

nodes.title: Is your involvement preference nonnegotiable?

question.text: Is your involvement preference nonnegotiable?
question.why_we_ask: Marking it nonnegotiable means it is a must-have for you to move forward.

choices.label: Yes
pros: Your involvement terms become a hard constraint
cons: Structures that need different involvement are excluded

choices.label: No
pros: Scenarios may adjust your role for a better overall fit
cons: Suggested paths may assume more or less involvement than you want

nodes.title: How important is employee ownership?

question.text: How important is employee ownership?
question.why_we_ask: Now that the system understands your priorities. If you choose Essential, employee ownership becomes nonnegotiable and the system does not need to ask this again later.

choices.label: Essential
pros: Employee ownership becomes nonnegotiable — every scenario must preserve it
cons: Paths without meaningful employee ownership are excluded

choices.label: Very important
pros: Scenarios favor structures with strong employee ownership
cons: A scenario may still trade some ownership for a goal you rank higher

choices.label: I'd like to explore it
pros: Employee-ownership structures stay in the comparison set
cons: No commitment — other paths remain equally live

choices.label: I'm open to other options
pros: The widest path set stays on the table
cons: Employee ownership may appear in fewer scenarios

nodes.title: Revenue

question.text: Which range describes your annual revenue?
question.why_we_ask: Start approximate. The system should not demand exact numbers this early unless they are necessary.

nodes.title: Approximate annual cash flow / EBITDA

question.text: Which range describes your approximate annual cash flow / EBITDA?

nodes.title: Number of employees

question.text: Which range describes your number of employees?

nodes.title: Existing business debt

question.text: How would you describe your existing business debt?

nodes.title: Ownership

question.text: How is the business owned today?

nodes.title: How dependent is the business on you personally?

question.text: How dependent is the business on you personally?
question.why_we_ask: This can materially affect the feasibility of different transition paths. A later scenario may note that owner dependency appears to be a significant issue your professional team may want to address before a transition — it should not automatically declare the business unsuitable.

choices.label: The business can operate without me
I'm important, but the team could take over

nodes.title: Do you have people who could help lead the company after you leave?

question.text: Do you have people who could help lead the company after you leave?

nodes.title: How interested do your employees appear to be in ownership?

question.text: How interested do your employees appear to be in ownership?
question.why_we_ask: This information becomes an input to scenario development.

nodes.title: How would you ideally like to receive the value from your business?

question.text: How would you ideally like to receive the value from your business?
question.why_we_ask: Only now does the application dive deeper into proceeds.

choices.label: Mostly cash at closing
pros: Certainty — value is set and paid at the closing table
Simplest to reinvest or diversify
cons: The total may be lower than structures that defer part of the price

choices.label: A mix of cash and future payments
pros: Cash at closing plus payments over time
cons: Part of your value depends on the buyer's future performance

choices.label: Mostly income over time
pros: Predictable personal cash flow for years
Retains upside during the payout period
cons: Depends on the buyer's continued performance
Full liquidity is delayed

nodes.title: Would you like to explore a specific target?

question.text: Would you like to explore a specific target?
question.why_we_ask: A quantitative threshold is introduced only where useful — the journey avoids demanding a number from someone who has no idea yet.

choices.label: Yes
pros: Scenarios can be tested against a concrete number
cons: An early target may need revision once valuation work begins

nodes.title: Approximately how much would you ideally like at closing?

question.text: Approximately how much would you ideally like at closing?

nodes.title: Would you like to explore seller financing?
nodes.body: One possible way to structure a transaction is for you to receive part of the purchase price over time through seller financing.

question.text: Would you like to explore that?
question.why_we_ask: Seller financing appears only when your answers make it relevant.

choices.label: Yes
pros: Part of the price can be structured as payments over time
Widens the set of workable structures
cons: Payments depend on the business's future performance
Your exit stays partially open until the note is paid

choices.label: Show me other options
pros: Exploration continues without a seller note
cons: The seller-note liquidity pathway is not opened

nodes.title: What would you want to do with the seller note?

question.text: What would you want to do with the seller note?
question.why_we_ask: This launches the Seller-Note Liquidity pathway.

choices.label: Keep it
pros: You hold the full remaining value and all future interest
cons: Payment risk stays with you, and the note is hard to sell or borrow against

choices.label: Explore selling part of it
pros: Part of the note becomes cash now while some payments keep coming
cons: Sold portions typically price below face value

choices.label: Explore selling all of it
pros: The full note becomes cash — no further payment risk
cons: All future payments and upside go to the buyer, at a discount

nodes.title: Ownership Structure Exploration
nodes.body: The platform now has enough context to surface potential structures. It selects the most relevant 2-3 rather than showing everything. Potential structures include: ESOP, Direct Employee Purchase, Management Buyout, Employee-Owned Acquisition Entity, Staged Employee Ownership, Other / Explore Alternatives. You can Explore, Compare, or Show Me Another Path. No structure becomes selected merely because it was displayed.

nodes.title: Scenario Builder
nodes.body: For each relevant scenario you see: what it is (plain-language explanation), why it appeared (tied to what you told us), current assumptions, potential characteristics, trade-offs, a must-have check against your nonnegotiables, and questions for your professionals. The platform does not call this a recommendation.

nodes.title: What-If Exploration
nodes.body: You can explore a small number of controlled adjustments — for example: What if you received less cash at closing? What if you stayed involved for 18 months instead of 6? What if you kept more of the seller note? You can compare the effect without losing the original scenario.

nodes.title: Scenario Compatibility
nodes.body: Every scenario receives a simple compatibility assessment against your own requirements: which nonnegotiables it appears to satisfy, and which assumptions may conflict. This is a constraint analysis, not a ranking.

nodes.title: Build the Professional Team
nodes.body: Your current plan involves several areas of specialized expertise: Attorney, CPA / tax professional, Valuation professional, Financing professional, ESOP professional, Trustee, Financial advisor, and other specialists. For each, the journey asks whether you already have someone.

nodes.title: Role-Fit Check
nodes.body: Your existing professional may be an important part of your team. Some transaction functions require specialized experience. The platform does not judge a professional's competence — it helps you consider whether the person's experience matches the role.

nodes.title: Your Professional Review Package
nodes.body: The platform now assembles the Owner's Employee Ownership Professional Review Package, opening with a one-page executive summary: what I want, my must-haves, my strong preferences, what I want to avoid, the paths I want evaluated, and my main questions for advisors — followed by thirteen sections from Owner Objective through Current Working Plan. The journey then becomes iterative: professional feedback can produce new questions, assumptions, scenarios, priorities, and a new package version.
